notes: On a bare `any` value: runtime key enumeration of the D1 dynamic object's bag, the index keys of a boxed array or TypedArray ([ADR-01284](../adr/01/ADR-01284.md)), `[]` for a boxed primitive, TypeError for null/undefined — matching JS ([TDD-00155](../tdd/TDD-00155.md) Stage 1)

Keys enumerate in ES own-property order (array-index keys ascending numeric first, then insertion order) across `Object.keys`/`values`/`entries`, `for...in`, spread and `JSON.stringify`, for static and dynamic objects alike ([ADR-00996](../adr/00/ADR-00996.md))

An omitted optional field (`x?: T`) is not a key — filtered at runtime by its presence, as `JSON.stringify` already did, by `Object.values`/`entries` and `for...in` too ([ADR-01063](../adr/01/ADR-01063.md), [ADR-01066](../adr/01/ADR-01066.md))

On a bare `any` value: the D1 dynamic object's enumerable own values (or an array's elements) as a dynamic array, TypeError for null/undefined, `[]` for a boxed primitive ([ADR-01077](../adr/01/ADR-01077.md))
On an array: its elements, in a new array ([ADR-01469](../adr/01/ADR-01469.md))
Returns real `[string, V]` tuples (`[string, any]` for a heterogeneous shape or a structural type, as TypeScript types it); destructure with `for (const [k, v] of Object.entries(obj))`

On a bare `any` value: a dynamic array of `[key, value]` pairs — the dynamic object's enumerable own entries in ES order, or an array's index/element pairs — TypeError for null/undefined, `[]` for a boxed primitive ([ADR-01077](../adr/01/ADR-01077.md))
On an array: its `[index, element]` pairs ([ADR-01469](../adr/01/ADR-01469.md))
A null-prototype object of arrays, as in Node ([ADR-01331](../adr/01/ADR-01331.md))
Mutates and returns `target`
An array target takes its sources' indices (and other own keys), growing as needed, and the result is the target array ([ADR-01485](../adr/01/ADR-01485.md))
With an `any` target or source, the copy runs on run-time properties (getters run; null and undefined sources skipped), and the result is `any` ([ADR-01237](../adr/01/ADR-01237.md))
A source property the target's type lacks is written onto the target, and the result (TypeScript's `T & U`) is `any` ([ADR-01714](../adr/01/ADR-01714.md))

caveats: Prototype machinery exists on **dynamic (`any`-typed) objects only** — statically-typed structs have no prototype link, and a boxed primitive's `getPrototypeOf` answers `null` (no primitive prototype objects)
notes: The D1 prototype chain ([TDD-00155](../tdd/TDD-00155.md) Stage 3, [ADR-00623](../adr/00/ADR-00623.md)): property reads and the `in` operator walk the chain (own shadows inherited; `delete` re-exposes the proto's value), writes/`Object.keys`/`JSON.stringify` stay own-table — matching JS. `for...in` walks the chain's enumerable keys, a nearer key shadowing (ADR-01737). `Object.create(proto|null, descriptors?)`, `get/setPrototypeOf` (a non-extensible object refuses a new prototype), the `__proto__` accessor (JS setter semantics: non-object values silently ignored), and the `{ __proto__: base }` literal form all work; a prototype cycle throws V8's `Cyclic __proto__ value`

A null prototype is tracked distinctly from an ordinary object's (unmodeled) `Object.prototype` link: such objects render `[Object: null prototype] { … }`, `Object.getPrototypeOf({})` is the shared `Object.prototype` object (not `null`), and `{ __proto__: null }` builds a null-prototype object ([ADR-01094](../adr/01/ADR-01094.md))

caveats: An accessor descriptor on a declared field of a statically typed object is a compile error
notes: Real property descriptors ([TDD-00155](../tdd/TDD-00155.md) Stage 5, [ADR-00629](../adr/00/ADR-00629.md)): spec create-defaults (absent attributes are false), non-configurable redefinition rules, data and accessor descriptor forms. Object-literal `get`/`set` compile to dynamic-ABI functions invoked with the original receiver (inherited getters through the prototype chain included); `Object.keys`/`for...in`/`JSON.stringify` honor enumerability (stringify and spread invoke getters); rejected writes/deletes throw module-strict JS TypeErrors
`Object.defineProperties`; a function's own properties take descriptors too ([ADR-01237](../adr/01/ADR-01237.md), [ADR-01232](../adr/01/ADR-01232.md))
`getOwnPropertyDescriptor` and `getOwnPropertyNames` of a statically typed object read its layout ([ADR-01331](../adr/01/ADR-01331.md))

Arrays, static objects and class instances take new properties with attributes and accessors beside their elements or layout, accessor elements included (`[ 1, [Getter], 3 ]`) ([ADR-01824](../adr/01/ADR-01824.md))

`Object.getOwnPropertySymbols` lists an object's own symbols, a class's symbol-keyed fields among them, and `Reflect.ownKeys` its string keys then its symbols; spread and `Object.assign` copy symbol-keyed properties ([ADR-01421](../adr/01/ADR-01421.md))

caveats: Traps not consulted: `apply`, `construct`, `defineProperty`, `getPrototypeOf`/`setPrototypeOf`, `isExtensible`/`preventExtensions` — those operations forward to the target ([ADR-01814](../adr/01/ADR-01814.md))
The target must be a dynamic object (an untyped/`any` literal); statically-typed structs can't be proxied
notes: `JSON.stringify` of a proxy runs its traps; `util.inspect` shows its target, as Node does

caveats: `Reflect.construct` with a `newTarget` other than the target throws a TypeError rather than constructing with that prototype

The metadata API (`defineMetadata`/`getMetadata`/`getOwnMetadata`/`hasMetadata`/`hasOwnMetadata`, TDD-00161 Stage 3) stores on a dynamic-object target and does not walk the prototype chain (so `get` == `getOwn`); `Reflect.metadata` as a decorator factory is rejected

Every form requires a dynamic (`any`-typed, or `-compat=js`) target: a statically-typed object operand is a clean compile-time rejection (strict mode does not widen a typed struct to a bag, [ADR-00630](../adr/00/ADR-00630.md)), including `get`/`has`

A `Map`, `Set`, `Date` or function value is rejected at compile time by `Object.freeze`/`seal`/`preventExtensions`/`isFrozen`/`isSealed`/`isExtensible` (Node accepts each; a `Date` is held as an unboxed number, with no header to record a level in)
notes: Real runtime enforcement, not a no-op: the integrity level lives in the object's header word, read at every field-write site, so a blocked write throws a catchable TypeError through any alias, on any thread ([ADR-00055](../adr/00/ADR-00055.md), [ADR-01831](../adr/01/ADR-01831.md))

An array, or a typed array without elements, freezes too: its level is in the header word before its shared header, and every mutation checks it, throwing V8's TypeErrors ([ADR-01331](../adr/01/ADR-01331.md))

A **dynamic** object freezes via its descriptor attributes instead ([ADR-00629](../adr/00/ADR-00629.md)): writes/adds/deletes throw, `Object.isFrozen`/`isSealed`/`isExtensible` answer truthfully; `Object.seal` and `Object.preventExtensions` enforce their own tiers the same way

A static object's shape is fixed at compile time, so seal enforces nothing further on it; it records the object's integrity level so `Object.isSealed`/`isFrozen`/`isExtensible` answer as in JS — as do `Object.preventExtensions` and `Object.freeze` ([ADR-01094](../adr/01/ADR-01094.md))

On a fixed-shape object a string-literal key is a compile-time answer — except an optional field (`x?: T`), whose answer is its runtime presence (`"age" in { name }` is `false`, ADR-01063); a runtime string key is compared against the object's own keys; a dictionary or `any` value is tested at run time ([ADR-01483](../adr/01/ADR-01483.md))

Returns a *dynamic object* (a `Map<string,V>`-backed value, [TDD-00012](../tdd/TDD-00012.md)); read via `obj.field`/`obj[key]`. Seeds via the same `[K,V][]` walker `new Map(entries)` uses ([ADR-00347](../adr/00/ADR-00347.md))
Other keys (a number, a symbol, an object; from an array or a `Map`) go through ToPropertyKey, into an `any` object ([ADR-01737](../adr/01/ADR-01737.md))

Spreading a bare `any` (`{ ...process.env, X: '1' }`, a `JSON.parse` result) builds the literal as a D1 dynamic object, since its key set exists only at run time; the result is `any` ([ADR-01077](../adr/01/ADR-01077.md))

A literal with a runtime key is built as JavaScript builds it, a dynamic object whose keys exist at run time: values of any types, methods (`q[k]()`, `q.name()`), getters, spreads and a declared index-signature type all work, and it can be held in `any` (the same object) ([ADR-01486](../adr/01/ADR-01486.md))

A well-known-symbol key (`[Symbol.iterator]`, `[Symbol.asyncIterator]`, `[Symbol.toPrimitive]`, …) in the colon, method, generator (`*[Symbol.iterator]()`) or async form desugars to a reserved *static* key, so the literal stays a static struct and the member drives iteration and conversion ([ADR-00279](../adr/00/ADR-00279.md), [ADR-01292](../adr/01/ADR-01292.md)); a computed name takes the method forms too (`{ [name]() {} }`, `async [name]() {}`)
Desugars to `{ foo: function() {...} }` — a plain anonymous function value, reusing the same closure machinery ([TDD-00060](../tdd/TDD-00060.md))
Generator and async-generator shorthands (`*g() {}`, `async *g() {}`, `*[Symbol.iterator]() {}`) read `this` as the receiver ([ADR-01737](../adr/01/ADR-01737.md))

`.get()` (`Map` and `WeakMap`) returns `V \| undefined` — a missing key reads as a real `undefined` (as in Node), distinguishable from a stored `0`/`false`/`""` via the presence-flagged nullable-scalar representation (scalar `V`) or the null-pointer miss typed `undefined` (pointer `V`); narrow / `?? d` / `!` before use ([TDD-00064](../tdd/TDD-00064.md)/[ADR-00833](../adr/00/ADR-00833.md)). (`URLSearchParams.get` is spec'd `string \| null` and keeps `null`.)

Keys of one kind pick a specialized runtime (string keys content-hashed, numeric keys raw-i64); a bare `new Map()` whose keys are **heterogeneous**, or a `new Map([...])` seed whose pairs differ in key or value type ([ADR-01830](../adr/01/ADR-01830.md)), widens to an any-keyed runtime with NaN-boxed keys/values and JS **SameValueZero** equality — string/number/NaN/boolean/object/array/`null`/`undefined` keys coexist, `NaN` matches `NaN`, and objects key by reference. Its values are `any` (boxed) ([TDD-00211](../tdd/TDD-00211.md)/[ADR-00932](../adr/00/ADR-00932.md))

An explicitly-typed **object/array-keyed** map (`Map<{…},V>`, `Map<T[],V>`) also rides the any-keyed runtime: keys box for reference identity (same reference round-trips through get/has/delete, a distinct reference of equal content is a different key), and `keys()`/`entries()`/`forEach` surface the live references ([ADR-00948](../adr/00/ADR-00948.md))

`keys()`, `values()` and `entries()` of a `Map` or `Set` return live iterators (`next()`, the iterator helpers ([ADR-01373](../adr/01/ADR-01373.md)), `for...of`, spread, `Array.from`): an entry added before the iterator reaches it is visited, a deleted one is not, and `console.log` shows the entries still to come (`[Map Iterator] { 'a' }`) ([ADR-01313](../adr/01/ADR-01313.md))

Calls `fn(value, key, map)`, matching real JS's full callback signature — the 3rd `map` argument is the map being iterated ([ADR-00573](../adr/00/ADR-00573.md)); a callback declaring fewer parameters just receives the leading ones ([ADR-00053](../adr/00/ADR-00053.md))
Resets size to 0 in place — doesn't free/reallocate the backing arrays ("leak by design" memory model); immediately reusable afterward ([ADR-00053](../adr/00/ADR-00053.md))

Takes any iterable of `[key, value]` pairs — an array, another `Map`, an iterator, a generator or an object with `[Symbol.iterator]` ([ADR-01313](../adr/01/ADR-01313.md)); K/V are inferred from the entries when no `<K, V>` is given; duplicate keys resolve last-wins ([TDD-00066](../tdd/TDD-00066.md))
Takes any iterable: an array, another `Set`, an iterator, a generator or an object with `[Symbol.iterator]` ([ADR-01313](../adr/01/ADR-01313.md))

An **object/array-typed** Set (`Set<{…}>`, `Set<T[]>`) rides the any-keyed runtime with reference identity — the same reference is one element, a distinct reference of equal content is another; iteration (`values`/`for…of`/`forEach`) surfaces the live references ([ADR-00948](../adr/00/ADR-00948.md))

Calls `fn(value, value, set)` — real JS's `Set.prototype.forEach` passes the value twice (Map/Set callback-shape parity) then the set itself; each argument is supplied per the callback's declared arity ([ADR-00053](../adr/00/ADR-00053.md)/[ADR-00573](../adr/00/ADR-00573.md))
Same in-place reset as `Map.clear()` ([ADR-00053](../adr/00/ADR-00053.md))

caveats: Under `-mm=manual` (default) a weak reference is strong: nothing is ever collected, so `.deref()` never becomes `undefined` and keys persist ("leak by design"). Real weak semantics require `-mm=gc` ([TDD-00112](../tdd/TDD-00112.md)/[ADR-00349](../adr/00/ADR-00349.md))
notes: `-mm=gc`: genuinely weak via Boehm disappearing links (the referent word is `GC_malloc_atomic`/unscanned so it isn't traced); a collected referent's `.deref()`/`WeakMap.has` observably drops. `gc()` (Node `--expose-gc` idiom) forces a full collection under gc, a no-op under manual

Keys are objects or unregistered symbols (`WeakKey`, as TypeScript's ES2023 lib); `new WeakMap(entries)`/`new WeakSet(values)` seed from an iterable, a primitive throwing the TypeError ([ADR-01737](../adr/01/ADR-01737.md))

`WeakRef` is a TypeScript class (`lib/node/kml_weakref.ts`): any object, function or unregistered symbol as target (`WeakRef: invalid target` otherwise), `.deref()` `undefined` once collected, its target kept alive to the end of the job that made or derefed it (the spec's kept objects), and V8's inspect output ([ADR-01366](../adr/01/ADR-01366.md))

segments.text: - Objects are fixed-shape heap structs — no dynamic property add/delete (`Object.freeze`/`.seal` don't need to enforce this; it's already structurally impossible).
